newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Mixed as crude falters.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Mixed as crude falters.

text.p: Singapore middle-distillate prices were mixed on Tuesday with physical gas oil steady to slightly lower, while jet fuel were discussed firmer in a quiet market, traders said.
Swaps gas oil fell along with weaker crude with August last quoted at $$21.20/$21.30 per barrel, from Monday's $21.35/$21.45.
Despite the higher offers on physical jet fuel, the August swaps regrade lost 30 cents to $1.50/$1.70 per barrel.
Traders said three gas oil cargoes have already been sold to a European trader for delivery to Argentina and Paraguay--one from a South Korean refiner and two from a European major.

While this have prompted other suppliers to consider shipping diesel to the latin continent, others said demand there was not large and they need products with special specifications which could be difficult to come by.
Nevertheless, the possibility has raised hopes of shipping cargoes to other regions and to soak up supplies.
Traders were also waiting for China's return as flood waters in southern China subsided, but most of its requirements would still be sourced from the well-supplied Hong Kong.

Gas oil for early August was offered a low as $20.50 per barrel. Taiwan was said to have sold two 0.3-percent sulphur gas oil cargoes at around $20.30 per barrel to a Swiss trader and a US major for August 5-10 lifting, free-on-board basis.
Taiwan's CPC sold one cargo in its last tender for end-July lifting at a 50-cent discount to Singapore spot quotes, fob.
Traders said jet fuel was offered higher at $23.20 for mid-August lifting. A buyer was keen to buy at this level but nothing was concluded. Another offer was seen at $22.85, fob basis.
